edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: I. Apprehensi sunt adolescentes catechumini, Revocatus et Felicitas conserva ejus, Saturninus et Secundulus. Inter quos et Vivia Perpetua, honeste nata, liberaliter instituta, matronaliter nupta, habens patrem et matrem et fratres duos, alterum aeque catechuminum, et filium infantem ad ubera. Erat autem ipsa annorum circiter viginti duorum. Haec ordinem totum martyrii sui jam hinc ipsa narrabit, sicut conscriptum manu sua et suo sensu reliquit. II. « Cum adhuc, inquit, cum persecutoribus essemus, et me pater avertere et dejicere pro sua affectione perseveraret: Pater, inquio, vides, verbi gratia, vas hoc jacens, urceolum, sive aliud? » Et « dixit: Video. » Et ego dixi ei: « Numquid alio nomine vocari potest quam quod est? » Et ait: « Non. » « Sic et ego aliud me dicere non possum, nisi quod sum Christiana. » Tunc pater motus in hoc verbo, misit « se in me ut oculos mihi erueret: sed vexavit tantum, et profectus est victus cum argumentis diaboli, Tunc paucis diebus quod caruissem patre, Domino gratias egi, et refrigeravit absentia illius. In ipso spatio paucorum dierum baptizati sumus; mihi autem Spiritus dictavit nihil aliud petendum in aqua, nisi sufferentiam carnis. Post paucos dies recipimur in carcerem, et expavi, quia numquam experta eram tales tenebras. O diem asperum! aestus validos turbarum beneficio concussurae militum: novissime macerabar sollicitudine infantis. Ibi tunc Tertius et Pomponius, benedicti diacones, qui nobis ministrabant, constituerunt praemio ut, paucis horis emissi, in meliorem locum carceris refrigeraremus. Tunc exeuntes de carcere universi sibi vacabant. Ego infantem lactabam jam inedia defectum. Sollicita pro eo adloquebar matrem, et confortabam fratrem, commendabam filium. Tabescebam ideo quod illos tabescere videram mei beneficio. Tales sollicitudines multis diebus passa sum, et usurpavi ut mecum infans in carcere maneret; et statim convalui, et relevata sum a labore et sollicitudine infantis: et factus est mihi carcer subito quasi praetorium, ut ibi mallem esse quam alibi. « III. Tunc dixit mihi frater meus: Domina soror, jam in magna dignitate es; et tanta ut postules visionem, et ostendatur tibi an passio sit, an commeatus. Et ego, quae me sciebam fabulari cum Domino, cujus beneficia tanta experta eram, fidenter repromisi ei dicens: « Crastina die tibi renuntiabo. » Et postulavi, et ostensum est mihi hoc: Video scalam auream mirae magnitudinis pertingentem usque ad coelum et angustam, per quam non nisi singuli ascendere possent: et in lateribus scalae omne genus ferramentorum infixum. Erant ibi gladii, lanceae, hami, machaerae; ut si quis negligenter, aut non sursum adtendens ascenderet, laniaretur et carnes ejus inhaererent ferramentis. Et erat sub ipsa scala draco cubans mirae magnitudinis, qui ascendentibus insidias parabat, et exterrebat ne ascenderent. Ascendit autem Saturus prior, qui postea se propter nos ultro tradiderat, et tunc cum adducti sumus, praesens non fuerat: et pervenit in caput scalae, et convertit se ad me, et dixit mihi: « Perpetua, sustineo te. Sed vide ne te mordeat draco ille. » Et dixi ego: « Non me nocebit in nomine Domini Jesu Christi. » Et de sub ipsa scala quasi timens me, lente elevavit caput: et cum primum gradum calcassem, calcavi illius caput. Et ascendi et vidi spatium horti immensum, et in medio horti sedentem hominem canum, in habitu pastoris, grandem, oves mulgentem; et circumstantes candidati millia multa. Et levavit caput et adspexit me, et dixit mihi: « Bene venisti, tecnon. » Et clamavit me, et de caseo quod mulgebat dedit mihi quasi buccellam, et ego accepi junctis manibus, et manducavi: et universi circumstantes dixerunt, Amen. Et ad sonum vocis experrecta sum, commanducans adhuc dulcis nescio quid. Et retuli statim fratri meo, et intelleximus passionem esse futuram: et coepimus nullam jam spem in saeculo habere.
pass_a_gloss: Young catechumens were seized, Revocatus and Felicity, his fellow servant, Saturninus and Secundulus, among whom also Vivia Perpetua, born well, educated liberally, married in a matronly way, having a father and a mother and two brothers, one of whom was also a catechumen, and an infant son at her breast, and she was about twenty-two years old, and she will now narrate the whole order of her martyrdom, as she left it written in her own hand and her own sense. While we still were with our persecutors, and my father was trying to turn me away and cast me down out of his affection, I said to my father, Father, do you see, for example, this vessel lying here, a little jug, or something else? And he said, I see, and I said to him, Can it be called by any other name than what it is? And he said, No, and I said to him, So I also cannot say that I am anything other than what I am, a Christian. Then my father, moved by this word, threw himself at me to gouge out my eyes, but he only harassed me and went away defeated, overcome by the devil's arguments. After a few days, when I had been without my father, I gave thanks to the Lord, and his absence was a relief to me. In that same space of a few days, we were baptized, and the Spirit dictated to me that I should ask for nothing else in the water except the endurance of the flesh. After a few days, we were taken back to prison, and I was terrified because I had never experienced such darkness, O harsh day, with strong heat and turmoil due to the benefit of the soldiers' disturbance, and finally I was worn out with worry about my infant. There, Tertius and Pomponius, blessed deacons, who were ministering to us, arranged for a reward that, having been released for a few hours, we might refresh ourselves in a better part of the prison. Then, going out of prison, everyone was taking care of themselves. I was nursing my infant, who was already failing due to lack of food. I was worried about him and spoke to my mother, and I comforted my brother, and I entrusted my son to him. I was wasting away because I saw them wasting away due to my benefit. I endured such worries for many days, and I managed that my infant might remain with me in prison, and immediately I recovered, and I was relieved of the labor and worry of my infant, and the prison suddenly became like a palace to me, so that I preferred to be there rather than anywhere else. Then my brother said to me, Lady sister, you are now in great dignity, and so great that you can ask for a vision and it will be shown to you whether you will undergo passion or reprieve. And I, who knew that I was speaking with the Lord, whose great benefits I had experienced, confidently promised him, saying, Tomorrow I will tell you. And I asked, and it was shown to me: I see a golden ladder of amazing size reaching up to heaven, narrow, so that only one person could ascend at a time, and on the sides of the ladder, every kind of iron tool was fixed, there were swords, lances, hooks, and swords, so that if someone were to ascend carelessly or not paying attention, they would be torn and their flesh would stick to the iron tools. And under the ladder, a dragon of amazing size was lying in wait, preparing ambushes for those ascending and frightening them so that they would not ascend. However, Saturus ascended first, who later had handed himself over voluntarily on our behalf, and at that time, when we were led away, he was not present, and he reached the top of the ladder and turned to me and said to me, Perpetua, I am waiting for you, but see that the dragon does not bite you. And I said to him, It will not harm me in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. And from under the ladder, as if fearing me, it slowly lifted its head, and when I had stepped on the first rung, I stepped on its head. And I ascended and saw a space of a garden, immense, and in the middle of the garden, a man of a dog-like appearance, sitting, dressed as a shepherd, large, milking sheep, and many thousands of white-robed candidates standing around. And he lifted his head and looked at me and said to me, You have come well, child. And he called me and gave me some of the cheese that he was milking, like a little mouthful, and I took it with joined hands and ate, and all those standing around said, Amen. And at the sound of the voice, I woke up, still chewing something sweet, I do not know what. And immediately I told my brother, and we understood that it would be a passion, and we began to have no hope in the world.

choices.english: a man of a dog-like appearance
choices.why: The Latin 'canum' means 'of a dog' or 'dog-like'.
The Latin 'urceolus' is a diminutive form of 'urceus', meaning 'jug'.
The Latin 'passio' refers to suffering or martyrdom.
The Latin 'saeculum' refers to the world or age.

pass_b_english: The authorities seized the young catechumens — Revocatus, Felicity his fellow servant, Saturninus, and Secundulus. Among them was also Vivia Perpetua, well-born, liberally educated, respectably married, with a father and mother and two brothers, one of whom was also a catechumen, and an infant son at her breast. She herself was about twenty-two years old. She will now narrate the whole order of her martyrdom, exactly as she left it written in her own hand and from her own understanding.

"While we were still with the persecutors," she says, "my father kept trying to turn me away and cast me down out of his affection. 'Father,' I said, 'do you see, for example, this vessel lying here, a little jug or something else?' He said, 'I see.' I said to him, 'Can it be called by any other name than what it is?' He said, 'No.' 'So I also cannot say that I am anything other than what I am, a Christian.'" Then her father, moved by this word, threw himself at her to gouge out her eyes; but he only harassed her and went away defeated, overcome by the devil's arguments. After a few days, when she had been without her father, she gave thanks to the Lord, and his absence was a relief to her. In that same space of a few days they were baptized, and the Spirit dictated to her that she should ask for nothing else in the water except the endurance of the flesh. After a few days they were taken back to prison, and she was terrified because she had never experienced such darkness. O harsh day! With strong heat and turmoil from the soldiers' rough handling; finally she was worn out with worry about her infant. There Tertius and Pomponius, blessed deacons who were ministering to them, arranged by a bribe that, once released for a few hours, they might refresh themselves in a better part of the prison. Then, going out of prison, everyone was free to attend to their own needs. She was nursing her infant, who was already failing from lack of food. Anxious about him, she spoke to her mother and comforted her brother, entrusting her son to him. She was wasting away because she saw them wasting away on her account. She endured such worries for many days, and she managed that her infant might remain with her in prison; and immediately she recovered, and was relieved of the labor and worry of her infant, and the prison suddenly became like a palace to her, so that she preferred to be there rather than anywhere else.

Then her brother said to her, 'Lady sister, you are now in great dignity, and so great that you can ask for a vision, and it will be shown to you whether you will undergo passion or reprieve.' And she, knowing that she was speaking with the Lord, whose great benefits she had experienced, confidently promised him, saying, 'Tomorrow I will tell you.' And she asked, and it was shown to her: She sees a golden ladder of amazing size reaching up to heaven, narrow, so that only one person can ascend at a time; and on the sides of the ladder every kind of iron tool is fixed — swords, lances, hooks, daggers — so that if anyone ascends carelessly or without looking upward, he will be torn and his flesh will cling to the iron tools. And under the ladder a dragon of amazing size lies in wait, preparing ambushes for those ascending and frightening them so they will not ascend. But Saturus ascended first, who later handed himself over voluntarily on their behalf, and at that time, when they were led away, he was not present; he reached the top of the ladder, turned to her, and said, 'Perpetua, I am waiting for you. But see that the dragon does not bite you.' She said, 'It will not harm me in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.' And from under the ladder, as if fearing her, it slowly lifted its head; and when she had stepped on the first rung, she stepped on its head. She ascended and saw an immense garden, and in the middle of the garden a man of dog-like appearance, seated, dressed as a shepherd, large, milking sheep; and around him many thousands of white-robed candidates stood. He lifted his head and looked at her and said, 'You have come well, child.' He called her and gave her some of the cheese he was milking, like a little morsel; she took it with joined hands and ate, and all those standing around said, 'Amen.' At the sound of the voice she awoke, still chewing something sweet she did not know. She told her brother at once, and they understood that a passion would follow; and they began to have no more hope in the world.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal translation, while Pass B provides a more fluent narrative version (shifting to third person where appropriate for the context of the story). Both correctly handle the specific vocabulary such as 'hominem canum' (man of a dog-like appearance), 'urceolum' (little jug), and 'caseo' (cheese). The distinction between 'passion' (martyrdom) and 'reprieve' (commeatus) is maintained. All clauses, including the description of the ladder and the dragon, are accounted for.
